$$

$k=${{field-1}}

feedback.problem:
The entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ k & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
equals $-1.$ Find the value of $k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ k & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-2(2k-0)+2(k-0) \\  & =-4k+2k \\  & =-2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{21}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{21} & =(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(4-2) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{21} \\  & =\frac{1}{-2k}\cdot (-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{12}^{′}=-1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{k} & =-1 \\ k & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
